intro: Shiloh's ministry has never stopped at the sanctuary door. Through the Faith Community Development Corporation — chartered by Shiloh and led by Pastor McCluster — the church has spent decades working on housing, economic development, sustainability, and justice for the City of Bridgeport.

items.title: The church that stood in the way — and won
items.body: United Illuminating's Docket 516R plan would have run high-voltage transmission monopoles through Bridgeport and Fairfield's residential and historic districts — threatening Shiloh's own building and the historic Mary & Eliza Freeman Houses. Anchored by Pastor McCluster, 85-year-old Shiloh became ground zero for the community's stand. Residents and clergy were joined by a bipartisan delegation including Senator Tony Hwang, Representative Jennifer Leeper, city council members, and Freeman Center president Maisa Tisdale, raising transparency and environmental-justice concerns the process had ignored.
items.outcome: On October 16, 2025 the Connecticut Siting Council voted 5–3 to deny the application. UI asked the Council to reconsider; on February 5, 2026 the Council rejected that appeal and closed Docket 516R. The community's unified front was recognized as a major factor in the decision.

items.title: The first African-American church in Connecticut to go solar
items.body: Freedom, Inc. partnered with Shiloh to make it the first African-American house of worship in Connecticut — and the first church in Southern Connecticut — to be completely powered by solar energy, with technical assistance and financing from the Connecticut Green Bank. Shiloh is a recognized Connecticut leader in the EPA's "God Goes Green" initiative, and the milestone launched Freedom's whole sustainability practice.
items.outcome: The "Shiloh Goes Solar" unveiling also announced Solar for All — a Freedom/PosiGen partnership backed by the CT Green Bank, described as the only zero-down-payment, no-credit-check solar program in the state.

items.title: The Shiloh Bethel Centre
items.body: A mixed-use apartment development in Bridgeport: 66 units across four floors over a podium level, on a footprint of roughly 16,500 square feet — 15 studios, 25 one-bedrooms and 20 two-bedrooms, plus 6 live/work units, about 4,000 square feet of commercial and retail space, 1,200 square feet of conference and office space, a 30-space parking garage and bicycle storage. Architect Powell & Partners uses a panelized, off-site prefabricated green building system that cuts waste and carbon footprint and brings units to market substantially faster than traditional development.
items.outcome: As the first church in Southern Connecticut on fully solar power, Shiloh intends to extend that renewable model from its South End facility into the Centre.

items.title: Faith Community Development Corporation
items.body: Chartered by Shiloh Baptist Church and led by Pastor McCluster as its President, Faith CDC carries the church's work into housing, economic development, and capacity building — training faith-based organizations nationwide in governance, program design, and revenue that renews itself, so a mission outlasts any single grant.

items.title: A voice for the city
items.body: Identified in the press as Shiloh's pastor, Rev. McCluster has been a founding member and organizer of Faith Acts for Education; pressed for a transparent Bridgeport police chief search; joined other clergy in charging that PSEG broke its promises to Bridgeport over the gas plant; called on the Connecticut legislature to act on the CCJEF school-funding decision; and took part in the Indiaspora Civil Rights Town Hall convened after the death of George Floyd, alongside DJ Patil, the first U.S. Chief Data Scientist, and Vanita Gupta, president and CEO of The Leadership Conference on Civil and Human Rights.

items.title: Bridgeport Regional Sustainability Summit
items.body: Shiloh hosted part of the 7th Annual Bridgeport Regional Sustainability Summit — "Learning to breathe easier and build better" — a full day of community training, a clergy luncheon, and an evening community conversation, held with the University of Bridgeport.
